items.reason: Pharmacological ascorbate is given IV at 87.5 g ("other names: ASCOR, vitamin C, ascorbic acid"). Manual §1.2 counts a licensed medicine given at pharmacological doses as pharmacological, and D30-R5 makes it a candidate when it is licensed as a medicine. That alone passes S6.

IV ascorbate is a licensed medicine (ASCOR) given as an investigational add-on with PFS, OS and RANO response outcomes. It is one of two investigational agents in each cohort, so rule 5 applies. D30-R5 requires the licensing evidence to be recorded in Table S2.
S6 is met by IV ascorbate whatever is decided about ferumoxytol ("All subjects will receive ferumoxytol and pharmacologic ascorbate in addition to the standard treatment").

Ferumoxytol is a registered drug added for every participant, and the primary outcome is "Ferumoxytol-related Dose Limiting Toxicities", with PFS, OS and response as secondaries. The record states no supportive, imaging or delivery purpose; the iron-deficiency text only justifies the dose. No antitumour mechanism is stated, so confidence is medium.
As for coder A's flag: a licensed medicine given IV at pharmacological doses is pharmacological and is a candidate under D30-R5.
The coders differ only in the label. The experimental arms contain "Radiation: External beam radiation therapy" and "Drug: Temozolomide"; the generic label "radiotherapy" is used.

note: Ferumoxytol's candidate status rests only on its being an investigational add-on with antitumour outcomes; no mechanism is stated. If XL instead treats it as non-antitumour, the trial still passes S6 through ascorbate. D30-R5 needs licensing evidence for IV ascorbate (ASCOR) in Table S2. Population is mixed because diffuse midline glioma is also eligible; 'Glioblastoma Multiforme' makes the terminology historical.
